worm.definition: A generally tubular invertebrate of the annelid phylum; an earthworm.

worn.definition: Form of wear (participle past): To have on.

worse.definition: Form of bad (comparative): Of low quality.

worship.definition: To reverence (a deity, etc.) with supreme respect and veneration; to perform religious exercises in honour of.

would.definition: Past tense of will; usually followed by a bare infinitive.

wouldst.definition: Form of will (archaic indicative past second-person singular): Used to express the future tense, sometimes with an implication of volition or determination when used in the first person. Compare shall.

wound.definition: Form of wind (participle past): To blow air through a wind instrument or horn to make a sound.

wrangle.definition: To convince or influence (someone) by arguing or contending.

wraths.definition: Form of wrath (plural): Great anger; (countable) an instance of this.

wreck.definition: Something or someone that has been ruined.

wrings.definition: Form of wring (indicative present singular third-person): Often followed by out: to squeeze or twist (something moist) tightly so that liquid is forced out.

wronged.definition: Form of wrong (participle past): To treat unjustly; to injure or harm; to do wrong by.

wrongs.definition: Form of wrong (plural): Something that is immoral or not good.

yards.definition: Form of yard (plural): A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.

yare.definition: Form of yair (alternative): An enclosure for catching salmon as the tide ebbs.

ye.definition: The Cyrillic letter Е, е, featured in various Slavic and Turkic languages.

year.definition: Form of here (pronunciation-spelling): This place; this location.

years.definition: Form of year (plural): A period of time akin to the time taken for the Earth to undergo a full cycle of seasons.

yes.definition: An affirmative expression; an answer that shows agreement or acceptance.

yet.definition: Thus far; up to the present; up to some unspecified time.

yield.definition: To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

yielded.definition: Form of yield (participle past): To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

yields.definition: Form of yield (indicative present singular third-person): To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.

you.definition: To address (a person) using the pronoun you (in the past, especially to use you rather than thou, when you was considered more formal).

young.definition: Offspring, especially the immature offspring of animals.

zenith.definition: The point in the sky vertically above a given position or observer; the point in the celestial sphere opposite the nadir.
